bearings.paper_claim: Katz prestige counts incoming directed paths. On one seed the Mental Health Act ranks 2nd at 2 layers (2,159 Acts) and outside the top 50 at 3 layers (6,021 Acts). Corrections Act moves 7th to 35th; Health Practitioners Competence Assurance Act moves 8th to 37th. The attenuation factor alpha is not reported.
bearings.paper_location: Sec. 3 p.12-14; Table 4 p.13; Table 2 p.9
bearings.system_side: kb_benchmark.py builds the kernel P with build_P on load_network(), which defaults to NET_CONFIG cu. It sums weighted OUT-walks, b = sum over k of (delta A)^k 1, with delta = 0.85 divided by the spectral radius, and writes kb_benchmark.json. The file calls itself a diagnostic not consumed by the chain, but make_member_desk.py reads it and shows a kb_pct percentile on the member desk.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Only the radius-sensitivity lesson transfers: ranks computed on a bounded subgraph are local. The paper's Katz counts in-paths (prestige) on an Act-citation graph, while the system's KB counts out-walks on a legislator kernel, so the paper does not validate the benchmark's direction. The transferable check is KB rank stability across cu and holistic, UNVERIFIED until reproduced (DE-062). KB values are heuristic model outputs, never influence probabilities (D-025).
bearings.verifier_note: Paper figures re-checked in the text and the code path confirmed. Rewrite the claim that the chain does not consume it: the file is not consumed by the chain, but the member desk displays a percentile from it. The alpha omission is confirmed.

bearings.paper_claim: Louvain on the LDA-based Act graph gives 14 communities at modularity 0.393 (two-layer) and 15 at 0.392 (three-layer). Modularity above 0.3 is treated as meaningful. Community-level Jaccard alignment with committee keyword sets runs 0.10 to 0.66. Agglomerative merging into 6 macro-communities raises the Maori Affairs match to 0.67.
bearings.system_side: press_hcoi.py builds member profiles over 19 curated press categories, links pairs at Pearson 0.6, runs Louvain with seed 7 and keeps communities of size 3 or more. It writes communities, profiles, edges and genealogy. It computes no modularity and no committee alignment score.
bearings.code_ref: fec/network/press_hcoi.py:4-5 (docstring pipeline), 64 (Louvain seed 7 and size filter); no modularity or Jaccard term anywhere in the file
bearings.transfer_conditions: Adding a modularity Q and an external alignment check, such as Jaccard against committee rosters or cosponsor communities, is cheap and transferable. The paper's Q and Jaccard values come from Act citation graphs and are not benchmarks for member press graphs. The weak committee alignment is a caution that topical communities need not match institutions. The homophily null result is cited from project memory and was not checked here.
bearings.verifier_note: Modularity and Louvain claims reproduced. The rel Jaccard range 0.10-0.67 is wrong at community level: 0.67 is a macro-community score in Table 6, and Table 5 tops out at 0.66. Merging moved only the Maori Affairs match (0.66 to 0.67).

bearings.paper_claim: Where the network boundary is drawn changes who is central: the top-10 Katz ranks reshuffle between the 2-layer and 3-layer subgraphs. The authors attribute part of the seed's 2-layer prominence to construction bias, since the seed is the root of the subgraph.
bearings.system_side: The NETWORKS registry defines separately bounded universes: cu (published), holistic, holistic_norm (directed), bank_reg (CRS subject terms) and crypto (title screen). build_sector_diagnostic.py reports pct_novel against published CU and flags a hub as dominated when the top degree is at least 3 times the second.
bearings.code_ref: fec/moneyball_core.py:391-410 (NETWORKS registry); fec/network/build_sector_diagnostic.py:351-352 (pct_novel), 390-411 (_concentration, dominated = top degree at least 3x second)
bearings.transfer_conditions: The abstract point transfers: cross-universe centralization comparisons depend on how each bill universe was screened. The paper bounds by citation hops from one seed, not by topic screen, so its effect size does not transfer. Any cross-config comparison must name its window and denominator. The bank_reg 76.1 percent novelty figure is a run output not checked here.
bearings.verifier_note: Registry and the 3x hub rule are reproduced in code. The bank_reg 76.1 percent novelty figure was not found in code and was not checked against output. Keep the mechanism claim only.

bearings.paper_claim: The authors argue against PageRank for legislative networks because its static formulation is sensitive to network growth, citing Mariani, Medo and Zhang 2015. No numerical comparison with PageRank is shown.
bearings.system_side: Staffer PageRank uses damping 0.85 as primary, with sensitivity runs at 0.70 and 0.95, on a layer-balanced transition operator with a group-balanced teleport vector.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Weak. The growth critique applies to citation networks, where older nodes accumulate in-links. A co-tenure graph takes the argument only if snapshots across vintages are compared. The paper offers an argument, not evidence. The co-tenure graph description comes from project context and was not checked here.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper citation and the absence of a numerical PageRank comparison confirmed. Damping values and teleport logic confirmed in code.

related.why: Item exists. Malaterre and Lareau's press HCoI pipeline (topic profiles, Pearson 0.6, Louvain) is the template for fec/network/press_hcoi.py, confirmed in the script docstring.
Item exists. Battaglini and Patacchini's out-direction Katz-Bonacich is what kb_benchmark.py implements; the paper's in-direction prestige is a different quantity, so the two should not be conflated.
Item exists. Porter et al. provide committee-network structure for the US House, the natural external reference for an equivalent committee-alignment check.
Item exists. Both are network-centrality studies of legislation; together they show that centrality conclusions depend on graph construction.
Item exists. Kim and Kunisky detect communities in lobbying networks, the actor-level setting that the citation-only Act graph does not cover.
Item exists. Aref and Neal partition signed legislator networks into coalitions, which is the coalition reading Paul wants. Note that signed_coalitions.py uses this method, not Louvain.

summary_issues: Overall: not refuted. Most paper figures check out in the text: Table 1 gives 0.96 and 0.89 against LLM 0.86 and 0.78; layer sizes are 27, 2159 and 6021 with coverage 0.15, 12.2 and 34.0 percent of 17,709; Louvain gives 14 and 15 communities at Q 0.393 and 0.392; Table 4 rank moves are as stated.
rel.summary_md gives Jaccard 0.10-0.67 for the communities. At community level Table 5 runs 0.10 to 0.66; 0.67 is the macro-community Maori Affairs score in Table 6.

rel.summary_md and ext.key_findings say the merge into macro-communities raises the matches. Only the Maori Affairs match moves (0.66 to 0.67). The other Table 6 values repeat or are reduced copies of Table 5 values.

rel.bearings transfer text says the chain does not consume kb_benchmark. The file's own comment says that, but make_member_desk.py reads kb_benchmark.json (lines 825, 843, 1152) and displays kb_pct on the member desk. Reword to: not consumed by the chain; shown as a member-desk percentile.

rel.paul_alignment item (2) and rel.flags say Louvain seeds the signed-coalition search (positive-Louvain seed). REFUTED: fec/network/signed_coalitions.py optimises an Aref-Neal frustration partition from a party-split seed and random restarts. Louvain appears in fec only in press_hcoi.py. Remove the claim.

ext.key_findings 2 and ext.limitations: the paper gives a deliberate trade-off between thematic relevance and processability as its first reason for the three-layer cut (Sec. 2.4 p.8). The top-50 loss is an observation alongside that. Also ext.limitations says temperature 0 gives consistent outputs; the paper says only limited lexical variation.

rel.paul_alignment item (3) says the system retired direction-blind cosponsor centrality (AB13 = 0) and that HCoI homophily came back null. Neither could be confirmed here: AB13 has no match in the fec Python tree and the homophily result was not checked. Treat both as unverified project history.

Confirmed internal inconsistency: rule-based precision is 93 percent in Sec. 2.3 p.7 but 0.96 in Table 1 p.8. Alpha, the Louvain resolution and seed, and the linkage are unreported, so Katz and Louvain results cannot be reproduced from the paper.

Confirmed: the NZLII reference is dated 31 June 2025 (text line 1170), which is not a valid date. Paul's margin note Important! Coalition on p.15 is present in the annotations. No separate ext or rel override files exist, so ext and rel were taken from the item JSON.
